c.v: According to whether clock domain crossing and synchronization are required, UART registers that can be configured by software are classified into three types, namely synchronous registers, static registers, and immediate registers.
Synchronous registers are read in Core Clock domain, and take effect after synchronization.
Static registers are also read in Core Clock domain, but would not change dynamically.

Therefore, for static registers, clock domain crossing is not required, and software can turn on and off the clock for the UART transmitter or receiver to ensure that the configuration sampled in Core Clock domain is correct.
Immediate registers are read in APB_CLK domain, and take effect after being configured via the APB bus.
